newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Iraq boats suspected of violating border zone - UN.
newsitem.headline: Iraq boats suspected of violating border zone - UN.

text.p: Several Iraqi boats suspected of carrying weapons have entered the demilitarised strip on the Kuwait-Iraq border, a United Nations official said on Thursday.
"They were Iraqi boats that seemed to have weapons," a spokesman for the United Nations Iraq-Kuwait Observation Mission (UNIKOM), said by telephone.
"They were observed by our helicopters last week," he added without elaboration.
After the 1991 Gulf War the United Nations declared a strip along the border between Kuwait and its former occupier Iraq whose troops were forced out of Kuwait by a U.S.-led coalition.
UNIKOM does not have boat patrols in the Khor Abdulla water passage in the border area, but its air patrols provide monitoring.
The incident has been reported to United Nations headquarters, the spokesman said.
Iraq invaded Kuwait in 1990 and annexed it for seven months before its Gulf War liberation.
